findings.description: Each call now clears and reuses the single shared statistics dict and binds it into the per-call copy, so overlapping calls of the same decorated function write into one dict and the second call's clear() wipes the first call's in-flight statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same decorated function at the same time, so the second call reaches stats.clear() while the first is still retrying. Mechanism: before this change each call's copy kept its own statistics dict and only the module-level attribute was rebound; now copy._local.statistics is the same object, so both calls mutate and clear it. Impact: the statistics seen by the concurrent callers (attempt_number, start_time, and similar) are silently wrong or reset mid-call.

findings.description: The async wrapper has the same shared-dict problem: stats.clear() and the shared binding into copy._local let overlapping asyncio tasks corrupt each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two asyncio tasks await the same decorated coroutine concurrently, so the second call runs stats.clear() while the first is awaiting between attempts. Mechanism: both copies write attempt and timing values into the one dict, and the clear resets the first task's counters. Impact: statistics read by either task are silently wrong.
